headline: Markets shut for Balipratipada; oil slides as Citi, HSBC turn bullish on India

segments.title: The big picture
segments.script:
Good morning. It's Tuesday, the tenth of November. Markets are shut today for Diwali Balipratipada, so this is a good morning to take stock after a busy festive weekend.

Three things matter most. First, Indian shares ended Monday at their highest level in more than eight months, and two big global houses, Citi and HSBC, have turned more positive on India. Second, oil is sliding hard. Brent was near 96 dollars a barrel during our session, and then fell more than 7 dollars a barrel in late American trade after President Trump signalled restraint on Iran. That is good news for our inflation, our rupee and our bond market. Third, Wall Street bounced back sharply from its worst week in nearly two years, even as Nvidia fell steeply over an investigation into its chief executive.

Let's take them one by one.

segments.title: How markets closed
segments.script:
Monday's session was a recovery story. After a volatile Muhurat trading session on Sunday, when the Sensex and Nifty gave up early gains to close in the red, Monday started weak as well. But the Nifty bounced more than 100 points from the day's low to close back above 25,000, up 0.23 percent. The Sensex recovered more than 400 points from its low to end 0.13 percent higher.

Banks did the heavy lifting. The Bank Nifty rose about 1 percent to trade above 59,500, and the public sector bank index gained between 2 and 3 percent, led by State Bank of India. HDFC Bank, ICICI Bank and Larsen and Toubro were also among the top Nifty gainers.

Pharma was the other bright spot, up about 1.5 percent on strong results. On the other side, information technology stocks fell more than 1 percent, even as global technology shares recovered. Mphasis, HCL Tech and Infosys lost 2 to 3 percent, and TCS was weak too. Tata Steel and UltraTech Cement were among the biggest Nifty losers.

Now to the money. Foreign portfolio investors have turned aggressive buyers. According to Choice Wealth, they bought a net 38,971 crore rupees of shares in the first week of November, after selling a net 34,843 crore rupees in October. Business Standard puts November buying by foreign investors at more than 4.1 billion dollars, and the Nifty rose more than 10 percent over the seven sessions to Friday.

For the charts, analysts quoted by Moneycontrol say the Nifty needs to close above the 25,150 to 25,200 zone to resume its uptrend towards 25,500, with 24,800 as the immediate support. For the Bank Nifty, the hurdle is around 60,400.

segments.title: IPOs and deals
segments.script:
In the primary market, Veritas Finance, a lender backed by Norwest Venture Partners and Kedaara Capital, has received the market regulator SEBI's approval for its public issue. It plans to raise 900 crore rupees through fresh shares, while existing shareholders will sell up to 1.28 crore shares. The fresh money will go to strengthen its capital base for lending.

In deals, Goldman Sachs has trimmed its stake in MK Sons Fine Jewels through a bulk deal, down from the 1.8 percent it held in September. And Zee Entertainment has risen 11 percent in two days, as its board prepares to consider a share buyback and a dividend.

segments.title: Results roundup
segments.script:
Now to results, and pharma stole the show. Divi's Laboratories has joined the 3 lakh crore rupee market value club, rising 15 percent in two days after its numbers and gaining for twelve straight sessions. JPMorgan kept its overweight rating and raised its target to 12,500 rupees. Sai Life Sciences jumped 9 percent to a record after its September quarter profit rose 17 percent to 98 crore rupees, on revenue up 23 percent at 659 crore rupees. Gland Pharma rallied 8 percent to a four-year high, and Laurus Labs and Glenmark also hit records.

In metals, Tata Steel's consolidated profit rose more than 16 percent to about 3,700 crore rupees, driven by India operations. Yet the shares slipped after a five-day rally, as brokerages stayed cautious about the British business. Nuvama upgraded the stock to buy with a target of 219 rupees.

On the consumer side, results were mixed. Jubilant FoodWorks fell around 5 percent after its quarterly profit dropped 43 percent. JPMorgan said fuel and wage inflation have stalled margin progress at Domino's, though Motilal Oswal remains positive on the medium term. Voltas reported a 51 percent jump in profit to about 48 crore rupees, on revenue up 15 percent at around 2,707 crore rupees, led by room air conditioners. Even so, the stock has fallen 8 percent over two sessions.

In financial services, Nuvama Wealth Management's profit rose 19 percent to about 304 crore rupees.

And Data Patterns rose 9 percent even though profit fell 55 percent, as management said it is confident of meeting this year's targets.

segments.title: Economy and policy
segments.script:
To the economy. The rupee broke a six-day winning streak on Monday. It touched a six-month high of 93.69 to the dollar, but closed slightly weaker at about 93.93, as state-run banks bought dollars. Bonds had a better day. The ten-year government bond yield fell nearly 4 basis points to 7.15 percent as oil eased, and foreign holdings of the fully accessible government bonds rose by nearly 8,000 crore rupees to 3.65 lakh crore rupees.

On the government side, central public sector companies have spent 5.03 lakh crore rupees on capital projects between April and October, up nearly 13 percent, and already 60 percent of this year's target.

Looking to the next Budget, an official says the government may announce support to boost domestic manufacturing of 100 products, including auto components, chemicals and machinery, to cut import dependence. The industry body FICCI, meanwhile, has asked for long-term capital gains tax on listed shares to be removed, with a higher securities transaction tax on delivery trades to make up the revenue.

On trade, India and the European Union have agreed to deepen cooperation in semiconductors, quantum technology and biotechnology, ahead of a proposed free trade agreement next month.

One worry from the farms. Rabi sowing is down 46 percent from last year, at 37.6 lakh hectares as of October the thirtieth, against 69 lakh hectares a year ago, after a 48 percent rainfall shortfall in October. Oilseeds and pulses are hit hardest.

segments.title: Around the world
segments.script:
Around the world, oil is the story. Prices fell more than 7 dollars a barrel in late trade on Monday after President Trump signalled restraint on Iran, and that lifted almost everything else. Gold crossed 4,100 dollars an ounce, helped by softer oil easing inflation worries.

On Wall Street, stocks rebounded from their worst week in nearly two years. The S and P 500 rose around 2 percent, its best day since April according to Moneycontrol, with all eleven sectors higher. The Nasdaq rallied more than 3 percent. Chipmakers surged, with AMD up more than 12 percent after Google Cloud chose its processors for new artificial intelligence systems, and Broadcom up more than 9 percent.

The exception was Nvidia. Its shares fell between 5 and 9 percent, depending on the report, after the company opened an investigation into chief executive Jensen Huang, following reports of a relationship with a woman suspected by American authorities of spying for China. Nvidia's board believes no secrets were compromised, and analysts say its upcoming earnings will be crucial. In Asia this morning, South Korea's Kospi jumped more than 5 percent in early trade.

And two big calls on India. HSBC has upgraded Indian shares to overweight and cut China to neutral, citing reasonable valuations, resilient earnings and strong credit growth. Citi sees the Nifty reaching 28,000 by the end of 2027, on earnings and lower oil prices.

segments.title: Your money
segments.script:
Finally, your money, starting with two useful tax rulings from the Income Tax Appellate Tribunal in Jaipur. In the first, an insurance agent's cash deposits of 35.09 lakh rupees during demonetisation had been treated as unexplained income. The tribunal deleted the addition after accepting records showing the cash came from policyholders' premiums. In the second, it deleted an 11 lakh rupee penalty on a farmer who accepted cash while selling his house for 22.5 lakh rupees, holding that his lack of awareness of the rules was a reasonable cause under section 273B.

If you bought gold this Dhanteras, note that mandatory hallmarking now covers six more districts, taking the total to 398 districts across 26 states and union territories. And the Reserve Bank has debunked a viral claim that existing cheque books become invalid after December the thirty-first.

For savers, Suryoday Small Finance Bank is offering senior citizens 8.6 percent on five-year deposits, with Jana and DCB Bank at 8 percent.

A warning too. Police in Hyderabad say a businessman lured about 7,400 investors with promises of 4 percent monthly returns, in an alleged fraud of 670 crore rupees. Returns like that are a red flag.

And bank branches are closed today in several cities, including Mumbai, Bengaluru and Ahmedabad.

That's the brief. Markets reopen tomorrow, Wednesday. Tonight, our time, the United States releases its October consumer inflation figures, and oil's slide will be tested against them. Watch whether the Nifty can clear 25,200 when trading resumes, whether foreign buying holds up, and India's own retail inflation numbers later this week. Have a calm and happy Balipratipada.
